$comment: The M1 item catalog, per design-bible §5. Volumes are cubic metres; cargo capacity is volumetric rather than slot-based, which is what makes bulk hauling a real profession.

items.name: Scrap Alloy
items.$comment: Hand-gatherable with no tool, so a brand-new character always has somewhere to start.
items.$priceComment: Whole credits per unit, like quest rewards. This is the floor that guarantees nobody is ever stuck: at zero credits a player can neither start a job nor place a sell order, since both charge up front, so ore would be unsellable exactly when it is all they own. Priced to be the worst option available -- selling to another player must always beat it, or the player market never forms. One credit against a 15 cr job fee means a few minutes of gathering unsticks you and nothing more.

items.name: Ferrite Ore
items.$priceComment: Twice scrap because it is tool-gated and slower to gather, but still a floor rather than a valuation. Twenty ore refines into four plates; if four plates ever sell for less than the 40 cr this pays, the floor has been set too high and the refining chain is pointless.

items.name: Ferrite Plate
items.$comment: Denser than its inputs by design: refining should make hauling easier, not harder.

items.name: Crude Thruster
items.$comment: The one intentional exception to everything being player-made. Bought from a faction supply order so the onboarding chain can complete before the electronics skill exists. Remove once players can manufacture thrusters.
